$comment: The WP5 native profile: one dedicated server and one matching native test
client, both running the same arena the browser slice runs.
scripts/arena_server.py derives every command line from the declarative
fields below and refuses this file if the committed argument lists differ,
so what the census observes cannot drift away from what is recorded here.
The profile is additionally bound to arena/game-profile.json and to
content/pack-recipe.json: the game directory, package, player presentation
and bot roster are the browser slice's and the pack's, not a second set of
values.
Neither the map NOR the per-server settings are here, and 'serverArguments'
carries none of them. The rotation, the gametype, the frag limit and the
bots are launch arguments supplied at container launch and never committed;
build the full command line with scripts/arena_server.py
server_launch_arguments, which prepends the rotation's own '+set d<N>' cycle
and '+vstr d1', adds the settings' own '+set' lines, and appends any named
bots' '+addbot' lines after the array below.
There is deliberately no committed default for any of them. A committed
value a caller may or may not override is a default nobody can see and
nothing reports -- the server would run a gametype or a frag limit its
operator never chose and would look exactly like one that was configured.
A server started without a rotation never answers a getstatus the readiness
contract accepts, so that omission fails the gate rather than surfacing at a
map change.
'launchSettings' publishes the bounds so a configuring consumer can read
them out of this authority instead of reimplementing the derivation; every
one of them is checked here against what derives it, because a published
bound is an assertion this repository is making.
The bot skill the census runs at is a launch setting now rather than a
committed difference: the census client is driven blind from a script and
would spend a session respawning rather than playing, so it launches its
server at the engine's lowest skill while the browser slice, played by a
person, commits 3. Bot skill changes how the game plays, not what the
protocol sends: it adds no message type, no command and no field.
runtimeBaseCopyrightFiles is the number of per-package copyright files the
pinned runtime base carries. The baseline's runtime-base record obliges
arena-web to preserve them, and preservation is checked by comparing the
built image with the base -- a comparison that would pass just as happily if
both sides silently dropped some, which is exactly what a `find` without
-L does here (two of the base's documentation directories are symlinks).
Pinning the count makes that regression fail instead of passing quietly.

cvarNotes.cl_allowDownload: 0 makes an attempted media download a visible failure rather than a silent fetch; WP5 must show that none is attempted.
cvarNotes.cl_motd: 0 structurally prevents the second-destination update-server request on every connect attempt.
cvarNotes.com_basegame: The same standalone game directory the server and the browser slice use.
cvarNotes.com_legacyprotocol: 0 is a CVAR_INIT profile bound: both rebuilt endpoints use the current checksummed netchan header.
cvarNotes.headmodel: ioq3 code/client/cl_main.c defaults it to sarge, which is retail Quake III data; CG_NewClientInfo then fails to register DEFAULT_MODEL and drops the client (code/cgame/cg_players.c).
cvarNotes.in_nograb: The census client runs on a virtual X server; grabbing the pointer there is pointless and would only add input noise.
cvarNotes.model: The same reason as headmodel, and the same player presentation the audited pack packages and the browser slice uses.
cvarNotes.name: A stable player name, so the server log and the census evidence identify the one human-slot client by name rather than as UnnamedPlayer.
cvarNotes.net_enabled: 1 is IPv4 only, so every observed datagram belongs to one address family.
cvarNotes.r_customheight: A small deterministic render size for the virtual display.
cvarNotes.r_customwidth: A small deterministic render size for the virtual display.
cvarNotes.r_fullscreen: 0 keeps the client inside the virtual display's own geometry.
cvarNotes.s_initsound: 0 because the census container has no audio device; sound has no effect on the wire.
cvarNotes.sv_pure: 0 mirrors the server: the QVMs are loose files beside the pack.

cvarNotes.bot_enable: Svcmd_AddBot_f returns immediately when it is 0 (ioq3 code/game/g_bot.c).
cvarNotes.com_basegame: Not baseq3. FS_CheckPak0 leaves com_standalone at 0 for ioquake3's own base game and the engine then refuses to start without the retail paks (code/qcommon/files.c). Any other directory name selects standalone operation.
cvarNotes.com_legacyprotocol: 0 is CVAR_INIT and forces the current checksummed netchan header on the matching client and server.
cvarNotes.dedicated: 1 is LAN dedicated. 2 would send heartbeats to the public master servers, which is an explicit WP5 non-goal (code/server/sv_main.c SV_MasterHeartbeat).
cvarNotes.net_enabled: 1 is IPv4 only, so the census observes exactly one address family.
cvarNotes.net_port: The UDP port the census captures; PORT_SERVER (code/qcommon/qcommon.h).
cvarNotes.sv_maxclients: Slots for the test client and the bots.
cvarNotes.sv_pure: Load-bearing: FS_FindVM only considers a loose vm/*.qvm while fs_numServerPaks is 0 (code/qcommon/files.c), and the QVMs are written beside the pack rather than inside it.
cvarNotes.sv_rateLimitPerPort: 1 is safe only on the managed relay path: the relay controls live source ports and gives concurrent clients separate connectionless buckets. An open-Internet server must leave this opt-in cvar at its default 0 because arbitrary source ports can evade limits and exhaust the finite bucket pool.
cvarNotes.timelimit: ioq3 code/game/g_main.c CheckExitRules: 0 means the frag limit alone ends a level. Both may not be 0, or no level would ever end and a rotation could never advance past its first map

engineCommandLineNotes.maxBytes: ioq3 code/sys/sys_main.c main() concatenates argv into char commandLine[MAX_STRING_CHARS] with Q_strcat, which truncates through Q_strncpyz rather than failing (code/qcommon/q_shared.c). This is the hard ceiling on how long a rotation may be; scripts/arena_server.py max_server_rotation reports how many of the published map names fit
engineCommandLineNotes.maxLines: ioq3 code/qcommon/common.c MAX_CONSOLE_LINES. Com_ParseCommandLine returns once it holds that many console lines, so a rotation past that point is silently not the rotation that was asked for

launchSettingNotes.bots: Exactly one shape. {"minPlayers": n, "skill": s} sets bot_minplayers and g_spSkill: the engine tops the server up and removes bots again as humans arrive (ioq3 code/game/g_bot.c G_CheckMinimumPlayers), costs two console lines whatever n is, and is the only shape that distributes across two teams -- where the same function clamps n to g_maxclients/2 - 1 per team. {"named": [{name, skill}, ...]} is the fine-grained alternative and costs one console line per bot. maxCount is the committed sv_maxclients less the human slot, which is also the clamp G_CheckMinimumPlayers applies in the FFA branch.
launchSettingNotes.fraglimit: The minimum is derived from the committed timelimit: CheckExitRules ends a level on a limit cvar and on nothing else (ioq3 code/game/g_main.c), capturelimit is unreachable below GT_CTF, and timelimit is committed 0 -- so a frag limit of 0 would commit a rotation that can never reach its second map. The maximum is a product decision rather than an engine one: three digits keep the widest launch line a fixed width, which is what makes the command-line byte budget predictable.
launchSettingNotes.gametype: GT_FFA and GT_TEAM, by name; the values are the pinned gamecode's own gametype_t enum (ioq3 code/game/bg_public.h) and are read from it rather than written here. GT_CTF is excluded because no published map is a CTF map, so it would be a content campaign rather than a mode switch.
launchSettingNotes.skill: 1..5, which is what Svcmd_AddBot_f clamps a bot's skill to (ioq3 code/game/g_bot.c). In the minPlayers shape it is g_spSkill, because G_AddRandomBot reads that cvar and passes it to addbot -- there is no per-bot argument to carry it there; in the named shape it is each bot's own third addbot argument.
